findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `pip install '.[eval]'` against a pyproject without an `eval` extra silently no-ops or errors, and either remove `eval` from the union spec or document why it is retained despite the extra being removed.
evidence: Plan text: 'change the joint lane to union:agents,eval,tracing,wiki'
tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py:47-53 — test_eval_extra_is_gone asserts 'eval' NOT in pyproject optional-dependencies

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'change the joint lane to union:agents,eval,tracing,wiki', but the 'eval' extra no longer exists in pyproject.toml (test_eval_extra_is_gone at tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py:47-53 explicitly asserts `"eval" not in extras`). Retaining 'eval' in the union spec means `pip install '.[eval]'` runs against a pyproject that has no such extra. Pip's behaviour with an undeclared extra varies by version and may silently succeed (treating it as the base package) or error. The plan inherits this pre-existing stale entry and propagates it into the new union string without noting that the install target is hollow.
findings.location: Dependency and CI section — '...change the joint lane to union:agents,eval,tracing,wiki'
scenarios: A future pip version that errors on an undeclared extra would break the union venv install, failing the optionality lane.
The wiki extra's joint-resolution guarantee is undermined if the union spec silently installs a different dependency set than declared.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact denominator for the rendered-character ratio (e.g., 'total source characters across all 178 bodies' vs 'total source characters belonging to eligible safe units') so test_dc_corpus_coverage can be implemented unambiguously.
evidence: 'Rendered-character ratio = source characters in successfully changed safe units / all source characters'
Numerator is scoped to safe units; denominator 'all source characters' is unscoped — creates two valid readings with different numeric outcomes against the ≥0.95 threshold
findings.finding: The denominator of the rendered-character ratio ('all source characters') is ambiguous: it could mean the sum of source characters across all 178 bodies, or the sum of source characters belonging only to safe units. Since the numerator counts 'source characters in successfully changed safe units,' a denominator of 'all 178 body characters' produces a different (and harder to reach) threshold than 'all safe-unit source characters,' and an implementer writing test_dc_corpus_coverage cannot resolve this without guessing.
findings.location: Corpus section — 'Rendered-character ratio = source characters in successfully changed safe units / all source characters'
scenarios: An implementer computes the ratio against total body characters and fails the ≥0.95 threshold because locked blocks, already-wiki units, and HTML-dangerous units are excluded from the numerator but included in the denominator.
An implementer computes it against safe-unit characters only, passes easily, but the intent was coverage across the whole body.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the definition to: 'Rendered-character ratio = Σ(source characters in successfully changed safe units) / Σ(source characters in all eligible safe units across all 178 bodies)', which makes the 0.984 measured value reachable and aligns numerator and denominator scopes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add Windows-compatible verification commands (e.g. `Set-Item Env:PATH ...` for PowerShell, or document that `make` with an activated venv suffices) or note that verification commands are Linux/macOS-only and point Windows developers to a documented alternative.
evidence: Plan text: 'Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`, `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`, and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test`.'
Windows CMD does not have an `env` builtin; PowerShell uses `$env:PATH` and `;` as separator; `$PWD` is a PowerShell-only automatic variable not available in CMD.
Windows is an explicitly listed platform in the supported client-shape matrix under 'Platform and venue'.
findings.finding: The Verification section prescribes `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint/typecheck/test` verbatim. `env` is a POSIX utility unavailable on Windows CMD; `$PWD` is not a CMD variable; the PATH separator `:` is wrong on Windows (must be `;`). A Windows developer following these exact verification commands will get an unrecognized-command error and cannot run the prescribed verification steps.
findings.location: Verification section — `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`
scenarios: Windows developer workstation (CMD): running `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` produces ''env' is not recognized as an internal or external command' and verification cannot proceed.

Windows developer workstation (PowerShell): `$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH` uses POSIX path separator; `make` may not be installed; the step fails or produces a wrong PATH, causing lint/typecheck/test to use the wrong Python environment.
